data.ruling: The refutation holds. The document key labels two datasheets with the wrong revision. [D9] reads "Nexperia 74LVC1G17 Rev. 15 (3 September 2024)". The datasheet at that URL is Rev. 16.1 of 3 September 2024. Rev. 15 is dated 2023-08-15. [D10] reads "Nexperia 74LVC1G04 Rev. 17 (4 August 2023)". The datasheet at that URL is Rev. 18.1 of 2 September 2024. Rev. 17 is a superseded revision. The re-rank's own saved copies, read at 2026-10-01T23:00:26Z, are byte-identical to my reads (MD5 checksums match), so the re-rank read Rev. 16.1 and Rev. 18.1 and mislabelled them. The correct labels are "[D9] Nexperia 74LVC1G17 Rev. 16.1 (3 September 2024)" and "[D10] Nexperia 74LVC1G04 Rev. 18.1 (2 September 2024)". The values the key serves are unaffected. The 74LVC1G04 Rev. 18.1 states CI 5 pF typical at VCC = 3.3 V (line 287 of the text extraction) and a Δt/ΔV row at 1.65 V to 2.7 V of 20 ns/V. The 2.7 V to 5.5 V row of 10 ns/V that the verifier cites is not quoted here; I did not extract it separately. The fault is a labelling error in the report figure. It is not about any part's lifecycle, notice, allowlist or LCSC identity, so the scope is function.
